summary: With verbs of knowing, wanting, being able, having to, being and feeling, the two pasts say different things. The imperfetto gives the state with its outcome left open (sapevo, volevo, dovevo, ero stanco); the passato prossimo gives the moment it began or what came of it (ho saputo: I found out; ho dovuto: I had to and did). Ask: was it the situation, or is it what happened?

subs.label: sapevo (I knew) or ho saputo (I found out)
subs.focus: Sapevo is the state of already having the information; ho saputo is the moment the news arrived, usually with a source or a time (da Maria, ieri, dal giornale, solo dopo). Typical error: the passato prossimo for I knew (Ho saputo già che eri malato) and the imperfetto for I heard, I found out (Ieri sapevo la notizia da Paolo). Items must show state or arrival of news with a word such as già, da tempo, non ... ancora against ieri, da + person, appena. Sapere + infinitive (non ho saputo rispondere: I was not able to answer) is a different use; do not test it against sapevo. Sapere against conoscere as vocabulary belongs to confused-verbs.

subs.label: conoscevo (I knew) or ho conosciuto (I met)
subs.focus: Conoscevo is already being acquainted with a person or familiar with a place; ho conosciuto is mainly the first meeting, with a place or a time (a una festa, l'anno scorso, a Londra). Typical error of English speakers: Conoscevo mia moglie all'università for I met my wife, and Ho conosciuto già Marco for I already knew Marco. Items give già, bene, da anni, non ... ancora for the state, or the place and time of the first meeting for the event. Incontrare against conoscere for meet belongs to confused-verbs.

subs.label: volevo (wanted, outcome open) or ho voluto (insisted and did), non ho voluto (refused)
subs.focus: Volevo gives the wish and does not say what came of it; very often a ma follows and it did not happen. Ho voluto says the wish was acted on (ha voluto pagare lui: he insisted and paid); non ho voluto is a refusal on that occasion. Typical error: the passato prossimo for a wish that came to nothing (Ho voluto telefonarti, ma non avevo il tuo numero). Items must state the outcome: ma + what stopped it for volevo; a result or a one-off decision for ho voluto. Non voleva as the description of an unwilling person is also correct Italian, so do not offer non voleva as a wrong sentence unless the frame clearly reports one finished refusal (Gli ho offerto un passaggio, ma non ha voluto).

subs.label: volevo for a polite request now
subs.focus: In a shop, at a counter or when opening a request, volevo softens a wish that holds now: Volevo un chilo di pane; Volevo chiederti una cosa. It is past in form only. Typical error: the passato prossimo (Ho voluto un caffè, per favore), which reports a past fact and is not a request, or reading volevo as I used to want. Items give a clear present request setting (buongiorno, per favore, scusi, a question that follows). Vorrei is just as correct, so never set volevo against vorrei; set it against ho voluto or against the bare voglio only for tone.

subs.label: potevo (was able or allowed) or ho potuto (managed), non ho potuto (did not manage)
subs.focus: Potevo gives ability, permission or possibility as a standing situation and does not say whether the thing was done: da bambino non potevo uscire la sera; potevamo scegliere. Ho potuto reports that on one occasion it was possible and was done; non ho potuto that it was not possible and was not done. Typical error: the imperfetto where the result is the point (Alla fine potevo parlare con il medico) and the passato prossimo for a standing permission (Da piccola non ho potuto guardare la televisione la sera). Non potevo for one occasion is common in speech as background (Ieri non potevo venire, lavoravo), so do not offer it as a wrong sentence; test affirmative results (alla fine, finalmente, per fortuna) and standing rules of an open period.

subs.label: dovevo (was supposed to) or ho dovuto (had to and did)
subs.focus: Dovevo gives the obligation or plan with the outcome open; with ma or però it usually means it did not happen (Dovevo studiare, ma sono uscito). Ho dovuto says the obligation was carried out; non ho dovuto that there was no need and it was not done. Typical error: the passato prossimo for was supposed to (Ho dovuto chiamarti ieri, ma mi sono dimenticato) and the imperfetto where the action clearly took place under pressure on one occasion (Ho perso l'autobus e dovevo prendere un taxi). Dovevo is also right for a repeated obligation of a past period (da bambino dovevo andare a letto presto); items must show which reading with ma, alla fine, così, or a habit frame.

subs.label: state or event with essere and avere: ero stanco, sono stato male; avevo paura, ho avuto paura; avevo dieci anni
subs.focus: The imperfetto gives how someone or something was while other things happened (ero stanco, avevo fame, avevo paura dei cani, ero a casa). The passato prossimo turns the state into an event: a closed stretch (sono stato male tutta la notte, ho avuto la febbre per tre giorni), a sudden onset or reaction (ho avuto paura: I got a fright), something that occurred or was received (ho avuto un'idea, ho avuto un problema), a visit (sono stato a Parigi due volte). Age in the past is normally imperfetto (avevo dieci anni). Typical errors: Ho avuto vent'anni quando..., Sono stato stanco e sono andato a letto, Avevo un'idea all'improvviso, Stavo male tutta la notte. Items need a frame that shows background beside an event, or a closed period, a count or a word of suddenness.

subs.label: c'era (there was, in the scene) or c'è stato (there was, it happened)
subs.focus: C'era and c'erano say what was present in the scene: c'era molta gente, c'erano due sedie, c'era il sole. C'è stato and ci sono stati report something that took place: an accident, a storm, a strike, a problem, a party, an earthquake. Typical error: c'era for the occurrence of an event that the sentence reports as news (Ieri c'era un incidente in centro) and c'è stato for furniture, people or weather as background (Nella stanza c'è stato un letto). C'era + event noun is possible as the scene of another event (C'era uno sciopero, così ho preso la macchina), so items reporting an event need a frame of news: ieri, stanotte, all'improvviso, with no second event leaning on it. Choosing c'è against è belongs to ce-or-e.

subs.label: pensavo, credevo, sembrava, mi piaceva against ho pensato, ho creduto, è sembrato, mi è piaciuto
subs.focus: Imperfetto for the opinion, impression or taste someone had over a time: pensavo di restare a casa, credevo di avere le chiavi, sembrava stanco, da bambino mi piaceva il latte. Passato prossimo for a thought that came at one moment or a verdict on one finished experience: ho pensato di chiamarti (it occurred to me), mi è sembrato strano, il film mi è piaciuto. Typical errors: Mi piaceva molto il film di ieri sera for the verdict after seeing it, Da bambino mi è piaciuto il gelato for a taste of a period, Ho pensato di avere ragione for a belief that turned out false. Items with piacere name one finished experience (the film last night, the dinner, the trip) or an open period (da bambino, a quel tempo). Keep the clause after pensare and credere to di + infinitive or a + noun so that the subjunctive is not needed; the syntax of piacere belongs to piacere-type-verbs.

subs.label: stavo per: was about to
subs.focus: Was about to do something in the past is stare per in the imperfetto: stavo per uscire quando ha telefonato Anna. The thing was on the point of happening and usually something cut in. Typical errors: the passato prossimo (Sono stato per uscire quando...), which is not used in ordinary Italian for this, and leaving out stare per (Uscivo quando...) where the action had not started. The event that cuts in is passato prossimo. Items test the form of stare, or stavo per against stavo + gerund only where the context makes clear the action had not yet begun.

rules.rule: If the person already had the information, use sapevo. If the sentence tells when or from whom the news came, use ho saputo: it means I found out, I heard.
rules.pattern: sapevo (già) che ... | ho saputo + da + person / ieri / solo dopo + che ...

examples.tl: Sapevo già che Marta abitava a Torino.
examples.en: I already knew that Marta lived in Turin.

examples.tl: Ho saputo la notizia da mia sorella.
examples.en: I heard the news from my sister.

examples.tl: Non sapevamo il suo indirizzo.
examples.en: We did not know his address.

examples.tl: Ieri abbiamo saputo che Luca ha cambiato lavoro.
examples.en: Yesterday we found out that Luca has changed jobs.

rules.note: With an infinitive, sapere means know how to, and its passato prossimo means managed on one occasion: Non ho saputo rispondere, I was not able to answer.

rules.rule: Conoscevo means I was already acquainted with a person or a place. Ho conosciuto, with a person, mainly means I met for the first time.
rules.pattern: conoscevo (già / bene) + person or place | ho conosciuto + person + place or time of the first meeting

examples.tl: Ho conosciuto mio marito a una festa.
examples.en: I met my husband at a party.

examples.tl: Conoscevo già Paola quando ho cominciato a lavorare qui.
examples.en: I already knew Paola when I started working here.

examples.tl: Non conoscevamo bene la città.
examples.en: We did not know the city well.

examples.tl: L'estate scorsa abbiamo conosciuto una coppia di Napoli.
examples.en: Last summer we met a couple from Naples.

rules.note: English uses two verbs, know and meet; Italian uses one verb and two tenses. For meeting someone you already know, by plan or by chance, Italian uses incontrare or vedere.

rules.rule: Volevo gives the wish and leaves the outcome open; it is the form to use when the wish came to nothing. Ho voluto means the person insisted and did it. Non ho voluto means the person refused.
rules.pattern: volevo + infinitive, ma ... | ho voluto + infinitive (and did) | non ho voluto + infinitive (refused)

examples.tl: Volevo telefonarti, ma non avevo il tuo numero.
examples.en: I wanted to phone you, but I did not have your number.

examples.tl: Mio padre ha voluto pagare la cena.
examples.en: My father insisted on paying for dinner.

examples.tl: Gli ho offerto un caffè, ma non ha voluto niente.
examples.en: I offered him a coffee, but he would not have anything.

examples.tl: Da piccola volevo fare la dottoressa.
examples.en: When I was little I wanted to be a doctor.

rules.note: Volevo does not say the wish failed; it only leaves the result unsaid. Volevo vederlo e sono andata a trovarlo is correct. English would not and refused to usually match non ho voluto.

rules.rule: To ask for something politely now, Italians often say volevo. It is a present request in a past form; the passato prossimo cannot do this job.
rules.pattern: (Buongiorno,) volevo + noun | volevo + infinitive (chiedere, sapere, prenotare ...)

examples.tl: Buongiorno, volevo due biglietti per Firenze.
examples.en: Good morning, I would like two tickets for Florence.

examples.tl: Scusi, volevo chiedere un'informazione.
examples.en: Excuse me, I wanted to ask for some information.

examples.tl: Volevo prenotare un tavolo per stasera.
examples.en: I would like to book a table for this evening.

rules.note: Vorrei is equally polite and equally correct. Voglio is not wrong grammar but sounds blunt to a stranger.

rules.rule: Potevo says that something was possible or allowed as a standing situation, without saying whether it was done. Ho potuto says that on one occasion it was possible and was done; non ho potuto says it was not possible and was not done.
rules.pattern: potevo + infinitive (ability, permission, open) | (alla fine / per fortuna) ho potuto + infinitive | non ho potuto + infinitive

examples.tl: Da bambino non potevo uscire la sera.
examples.en: As a child I was not allowed to go out in the evening.

examples.tl: Alla fine ho potuto parlare con il medico.
examples.en: In the end I was able to speak to the doctor.

examples.tl: Non ho potuto finire il lavoro ieri.
examples.en: I could not finish the work yesterday.

examples.tl: In quell'albergo potevamo fare colazione in camera.
examples.en: In that hotel we could have breakfast in our room.

rules.note: English could covers both. For a single occasion Italians also say non potevo when they are giving the situation as background (Ieri non potevo venire, lavoravo); the affirmative result, managed to, is ho potuto.

rules.rule: Dovevo means was supposed to, with the outcome open; followed by ma it usually did not happen. Ho dovuto means the obligation was met: had to and did.
rules.pattern: dovevo + infinitive, ma ... | ho dovuto + infinitive (and did) | non ho dovuto + infinitive (no need, and did not)

examples.tl: Dovevo studiare, ma sono uscito con gli amici.
examples.en: I was supposed to study, but I went out with my friends.

examples.tl: Ho perso l'autobus e ho dovuto prendere un taxi.
examples.en: I missed the bus and had to take a taxi.

examples.tl: Ieri Anna ha dovuto lavorare fino a tardi.
examples.en: Yesterday Anna had to work late.

examples.tl: Il treno doveva partire alle nove.
examples.en: The train was supposed to leave at nine.

rules.note: Dovevo is also the form for an obligation repeated over a past period, where the action did take place: Da bambina dovevo andare a letto presto.

rules.rule: Use the imperfetto of essere and avere for how someone was or felt while other things happened. Use the passato prossimo when the state has a closed length, or when it is something that came over the person at one moment.
rules.pattern: ero / avevo + state (background) | sono stato / ho avuto + state + tutta la notte, per tre giorni | all'improvviso + ho avuto ...

examples.tl: Ero stanco e sono andato a letto presto.
examples.en: I was tired and went to bed early.

examples.tl: Sono stato male tutta la notte.
examples.en: I was ill all night.

examples.tl: Da piccola avevo paura dei cani.
examples.en: When I was little I was afraid of dogs.

examples.tl: Quando ho visto il cane, ho avuto paura.
examples.en: When I saw the dog, I got scared.

rules.note: The closed length is what calls for the passato prossimo, as with action verbs: Ho avuto la febbre per tre giorni, but Avevo la febbre e non sono uscito.

rules.rule: Age at a past moment is given with avevo, and where someone was as background with ero. Ho avuto with a noun usually means got or had happen to me, and sono stato with a place means went and came back.
rules.pattern: avevo + number + anni | ho avuto + un'idea, un problema, una bella notizia | sono stato a + place (+ due volte, l'anno scorso)

examples.tl: Avevo vent'anni quando ho comprato la prima macchina.
examples.en: I was twenty when I bought my first car.

examples.tl: Stamattina ho avuto un'idea.
examples.en: This morning I had an idea.

examples.tl: Sono stata a Parigi due volte.
examples.en: I have been to Paris twice.

examples.tl: Ero a casa quando è arrivato il pacco.
examples.en: I was at home when the parcel arrived.

rules.note: The birthday itself is an event with another verb: Ieri ho compiuto trent'anni.

rules.rule: C'era and c'erano say what was there in the scene. C'è stato and ci sono stati say that something took place.
rules.pattern: c'era / c'erano + people, things, weather | c'è stato / c'è stata / ci sono stati + un incidente, uno sciopero, un temporale, problemi

examples.tl: Ieri c'è stato un incidente in centro.
examples.en: Yesterday there was an accident in the centre.

examples.tl: Alla festa c'era molta gente.
examples.en: There were a lot of people at the party.

examples.tl: Stanotte c'è stato un forte temporale.
examples.en: Last night there was a heavy storm.

examples.tl: Nella stanza c'erano due letti e un tavolo.
examples.en: In the room there were two beds and a table.

rules.note: An event noun can still take c'era when it is the backdrop to something else: C'era uno sciopero, così ho preso la macchina. The participle agrees with what there was: c'è stata una festa, ci sono stati dei problemi.

rules.rule: For a verdict on one finished experience, such as a film, a meal or a trip, use mi è piaciuto. For a taste someone had over a period, use mi piaceva.
rules.pattern: noun (one experience) + mi è piaciuto / piaciuta / piaciuti / piaciute | da bambino, a quel tempo + mi piaceva / piacevano

examples.tl: Il film di ieri sera mi è piaciuto molto.
examples.en: I really liked the film last night.

examples.tl: Da bambino non mi piacevano le verdure.
examples.en: As a child I did not like vegetables.

examples.tl: Ti è piaciuta la cena?
examples.en: Did you like the dinner?

examples.tl: A scuola mi piaceva molto la storia.
examples.en: At school I liked history a lot.

rules.note: Mi piaceva can also describe liking something while it was going on, as background: La casa mi piaceva, ma costava troppo. The verdict after the experience is over is mi è piaciuto.

rules.rule: Pensavo, credevo and sembrava give the opinion or impression someone had over a time, often one that proved wrong. Ho pensato and mi è sembrato give a thought or impression that came at one moment.
rules.pattern: pensavo / credevo + di + infinitive | sembrava + adjective | ho pensato + di + infinitive / a + noun | mi è sembrato + adjective

examples.tl: Credevo di avere le chiavi in borsa.
examples.en: I thought I had the keys in my bag.

examples.tl: Ho visto il tuo messaggio e ho pensato di chiamarti.
examples.en: I saw your message and thought I would call you.

examples.tl: Ieri Giulia sembrava molto stanca.
examples.en: Yesterday Giulia looked very tired.

examples.tl: Il suo comportamento mi è sembrato strano.
examples.en: His behaviour struck me as strange.

rules.note: English I thought is both. If you can say I was under the impression, use pensavo or credevo; if you can say it occurred to me or I decided, use ho pensato.

rules.rule: Was about to is stavo per + infinitive. In the past, stare per is used in the imperfetto; the event that cuts in is passato prossimo.
rules.pattern: stavo / stavi / stava per + infinitive + quando + passato prossimo

examples.tl: Stavo per uscire quando ha telefonato Anna.
examples.en: I was about to go out when Anna phoned.

examples.tl: Il treno stava per partire.
examples.en: The train was about to leave.

examples.tl: Stavamo per andare a letto quando è arrivato Paolo.
examples.en: We were about to go to bed when Paolo arrived.

rules.note: Stavo per uscire means the action had not started yet. Stavo uscendo and uscivo mean it was already under way.

contrasts.wrong: Conoscevo mia moglie a una festa di amici.

right.tl: Ho conosciuto mia moglie a una festa di amici.
right.en: I met my wife at a party given by friends.

contrasts.why: A first meeting at a named place is an event: ho conosciuto. Conoscevo would mean I was already acquainted with her, which does not fit a place of meeting.

contrasts.wrong: Ieri sapevo da Paolo che ti sei sposato.

right.tl: Ieri ho saputo da Paolo che ti sei sposato.
right.en: Yesterday I heard from Paolo that you got married.

contrasts.why: Ieri and da Paolo give the moment and the source of the news, so this is finding out: ho saputo. Sapevo is for information the person already had.

contrasts.wrong: Non ti ho detto niente perché l'ho già saputo.

right.tl: Non ti ho detto niente perché lo sapevo già.
right.en: I did not tell you anything because I already knew.

contrasts.why: Already having the information is a state and the reason for the other action: sapevo. Ho saputo would report the moment of learning it.

contrasts.wrong: Ho voluto chiamarti, ma avevo il telefono scarico.

right.tl: Volevo chiamarti, ma avevo il telefono scarico.
right.en: I wanted to call you, but my phone was dead.

contrasts.why: The wish was not carried out, so it stays a wish: volevo. Ho voluto chiamarti says the person insisted and did call, which the ma clause contradicts.

contrasts.wrong: Ho dovuto chiamare il medico ieri, ma mi sono dimenticato.

right.tl: Dovevo chiamare il medico ieri, ma mi sono dimenticato.
right.en: I was supposed to call the doctor yesterday, but I forgot.

contrasts.why: The call was not made, so this is was supposed to: dovevo. Ho dovuto means the obligation was carried out.

contrasts.wrong: Dopo due ore di fila, finalmente potevamo entrare nel museo.

right.tl: Dopo due ore di fila, finalmente abbiamo potuto entrare nel museo.
right.en: After two hours in the queue, we were finally able to get into the museum.

contrasts.why: Finalmente reports the result on one occasion: they managed and went in. That is ho potuto; potevamo would only say entry was allowed, not that it happened.

contrasts.wrong: Ho avuto otto anni quando è nato mio fratello.

right.tl: Avevo otto anni quando è nato mio fratello.
right.en: I was eight when my brother was born.

contrasts.why: Age is the background to the event, not something that happened: avevo. Note also that Italian has age with avere, not essere.

contrasts.wrong: Stavo male tutta la notte e stamattina non sono andata al lavoro.

right.tl: Sono stata male tutta la notte e stamattina non sono andata al lavoro.
right.en: I was ill all night and this morning I did not go to work.

contrasts.why: Tutta la notte closes the period and the sentence sums it up as a whole, so the state is told as an event: sono stata male.

contrasts.wrong: Mi piaceva molto il ristorante di ieri sera, grazie.

right.tl: Mi è piaciuto molto il ristorante di ieri sera, grazie.
right.en: I really liked the restaurant last night, thank you.

contrasts.why: A verdict on one finished evening is passato prossimo: mi è piaciuto. Mi piaceva is for a taste held over a period, as in da bambino mi piaceva.

contrasts.wrong: Sono stato per uscire quando ha cominciato a piovere.

right.tl: Stavo per uscire quando ha cominciato a piovere.
right.en: I was about to go out when it started to rain.

contrasts.why: Being on the point of doing something is a situation that the rain cut into: stavo per. The passato prossimo of stare per is not used for this in ordinary Italian.

cheat: Situation, outcome not said: imperfetto. What happened or what came of it: passato prossimo.
knew: sapevo, conoscevo. found out: ho saputo. met for the first time: ho conosciuto.
volevo, dovevo, potevo + ma: it did not happen. ho voluto, ho dovuto, ho potuto: it was done.
non ho voluto: refused. non ho potuto: did not manage. non ho dovuto: no need, did not.
Age, feelings and looks as background: avevo, ero, sembrava. Closed length or sudden onset: ho avuto, sono stato.
c'era: it was there in the scene. c'è stato: it took place.
Verdict on one film, meal or trip: mi è piaciuto. Polite request now: volevo. About to: stavo per.
